lines.text: Your diplomas.
A diploma from your own country is not the same as a diploma in the Netherlands (for example: university in your country = perhaps hbo level here).
You can have your diplomas evaluated [waarderen] at the IDW (internationale diplomawaardering).
If you must do civic integration [inburgeren] or want to apply for Dutch nationality [nationaliteit], this is free [gratis].
Programmes and courses.
You can always keep studying: for example become an mbo mechanic and then move up [doorstromen] to the hbo.
With an evaluated diploma (for example mbo level 3) and Dutch at B1 level, you can do an mbo 3 programme here.
There are also shorter courses; if you have a job, further training [bijscholing] is very normal — courses to keep up with new developments in your profession.
Language level for a study programme.
Some programmes are in English (for example at the university).
For a programme in Dutch: for mbo levels 1, 2 and 3, language level B1 is enough; for mbo level 4, the hbo and the wo you must have at least B2.
Language level for work.
In many professions you must be able to communicate well with colleagues, patients or customers.
Do you work in childcare [kinderopvang]?
Then language level B2 is mandatory.

For some jobs you do not need to speak Dutch: as a knowledge migrant [kennismigrant] (also called an expat) you can usually communicate in English; as a labour migrant [arbeidsmigrant] — for example in construction — you may not need much Dutch or English.
The situation in your region.
In a city there are often more study programmes.
Is the programme far away?
Then you must travel or perhaps move.
On the internet you can search for information per city.
